topicName: Compute Engine: Networking (VPC, Subnets, Firewalls, Routes)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Compute Engine: Networking (VPC, Subnets, Firewalls, Routes) in Google Cloud (GCP)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a comprehensive overview of networking concepts within Google Compute Engine, focusing on Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs), subnets, firewalls, and routes. Understanding these components is crucial for building secure and scalable applications on GCP."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network enables you to provision a logically isolated section of the Google Cloud Platform where you can launch Google Cloud resources. VPC networks are global, meaning they can span multiple regions without being tied to a specific region. A VPC network provides connectivity for your Compute Engine virtual machine (VM) instances, Kubernetes Engine clusters, and App Engine flexible environment instances."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Global Scope: VPC networks are global resources, not regional."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Connectivity: Provides connectivity between your GCP resources."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Isolation: Logically isolates your resources from other GCP users."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a VPC Network"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can create a VPC network using the Google Cloud Console, the `gcloud` command-line tool, or the Cloud Client Libraries. When creating a VPC, you can choose between auto mode and custom mode. Auto mode VPCs automatically create subnets in each region, while custom mode VPCs require you to define your own subnets."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"# Create a custom mode VPC network
gcloud compute networks create my-custom-vpc --subnet-mode=custom"},{"order":11,"type":"heading","text":"Subnets"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Subnets are regional resources that define a range of IP addresses within a VPC network. Each subnet has a primary IP address range, and you can optionally define secondary IP address ranges for use by services like Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). VMs within the same subnet can communicate with each other directly using their internal IP addresses."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regional Scope: Subnets are regional resources."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"IP Address Ranges: Define a range of IP addresses for resources within the subnet."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Internal Communication: VMs within the same subnet can communicate directly."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Subnet"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can create a subnet using the Google Cloud Console, the `gcloud` command-line tool, or the Cloud Client Libraries. When creating a subnet, you must specify the VPC network it belongs to, the region, and the primary IP address range."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"# Create a subnet in the us-central1 region
gcloud compute networks subnets create my-subnet \
    --network=my-custom-vpc \
    --region=us-central1 \
    --range=10.10.10.0/24"},{"order":19,"type":"heading","text":"Firewalls"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Firewall rules control network traffic to and from your VMs. You can create firewall rules that allow or deny traffic based on source IP address, destination IP address, protocol, and port. Firewall rules are defined at the VPC network level and apply to all VMs within that network."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"VPC Level: Firewall rules are defined at the VPC network level."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Traffic Control: Allow or deny traffic based on various criteria."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implicit Rules: GCP provides implicit allow egress and deny ingress rules."},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Firewall Rule"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can create a firewall rule using the Google Cloud Console, the `gcloud` command-line tool, or the Cloud Client Libraries. When creating a firewall rule, you must specify the VPC network it applies to, the direction of traffic (ingress or egress), the action to take (allow or deny), and the source or destination criteria."},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"# Allow ingress traffic on port 80 from any source
gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-http \
    --network=my-custom-vpc \
    --allow=tcp:80 \
    --source-ranges=0.0.0.0/0"},{"order":27,"type":"heading","text":"Routes"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"Routes define the path that network traffic takes from a VM instance to a destination. Each VPC network has a default route that directs traffic to the internet gateway. You can create custom routes to override the default route and direct traffic to other destinations, such as other VPC networks or on-premises networks."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Traffic Path: Define the path for network traffic."},{"order":30,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Default Route: Each VPC has a default route to the internet gateway."},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Custom Routes: Override the default route for specific destinations."},{"order":32,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Route"},{"order":33,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can create a route using the Google Cloud Console, the `gcloud` command-line tool, or the Cloud Client Libraries. When creating a route, you must specify the VPC network it applies to, the destination IP address range, and the next hop (e.g., a VM instance, a VPN gateway, or an internet gateway)."},{"order":34,"type":"code","text":"# Create a route to send traffic to a specific VM instance
gcloud compute routes create my-route \
    --network=my-custom-vpc \
    --destination-range=10.20.30.0/24 \
    --next-hop-instance=my-instance \
    --next-hop-instance-zone=us-central1-a"},{"order":35,"type":"paragraph","text":"By understanding and utilizing VPCs, subnets, firewalls, and routes, you can effectively manage and secure your network infrastructure within Google Compute Engine."}]
